title: Scalar is Not Enough: Vectorization-based Unbiased Learning to Rank

problem.claim: Unbiased learning to rank aims to train an unbiased ranking model from biased user click logs.

gap.claim: Existing examination-hypothesis approaches use independent scalar factorization, but practical interactions among features, bias factors, and clicks may violate this assumption and cause model misspecification and approximation error.

narrative_sequence.summary: ULTR seeks to learn unbiased ranking models from biased click logs.
Most ULTR methods rely on the examination hypothesis, which factorizes click probability into scalar functions for ranking features and bias factors.
Real-world feature, bias, and click interactions are complicated, making the scalar independent factorization potentially misspecified and error-prone.

source_observation.claim: A scalar independent factorization may fail when features, bias factors, and clicks interact in complicated ways.

interpretation.claim: Modeling assumptions that separate interacting factors should be treated as potential sources of misspecification.

application.claim: When designing click-based ranking models, examine whether the data support the assumed independence and factorization structure.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not state when the scalar factorization is adequate.

unknowns: The proposed vectorization-based method is not described.
No experiments, datasets, metrics, or quantitative results are supplied.
